## Scripts for small RNA processing & analysis

This document records the tools and scripts I used for the small RNA analysis

## Processing

Before the analysis, we did a few processing and filtering steps to remove non-relevant components such as adaptors, rRNA, tRNA, reads in low complexity regions,etc.

# Trimgalore

``` bash
trim_galore \
--small_rna \
--length 17 \
--output_dir /DIR_output \
--fastqc_args "--outdir /DIR_fastqc_output" \
--cores 4 \
--gzip \
--2colour 20 \
file.fq.gz
```

### Prinseq

This is to remove low complexity reads. Output would be good.fq and bad.fq

``` bash
zcat trimmed.fq.gz | \
prinseq-lite.pl \
-lc_method dust \
-lc_threshold 40 \
-fastq stdin
```

### Remove tRNA and rRNA

For this, we first download the tRNA and rRNA sequences from Rfam database using esl-sfetch

``` bash
module load DBD-mysql/4.055-GCC-15.2.0
module load Infernal
perl -MDBI -MDBD::mysql   -e 'print "DBI $DBI::VERSION; DBD::mysql $DBD::mysql::VERSION\n"'
esl-sfetch -h
esl-sfetch --index /home/cenliau/00_nesi_projects/brins03581_nobackup/Cen/Rfam.fa
```

Then use this perl script to extract the tRNA and rRNA sequences get_vitis_rfam.pl

``` bash
chmod +x get_vitis_rfam.pl

cd /DIR
./get_vitis_rfam.pl
mkdir -p tRNA
mkdir -p rRNA

for file in /DIR/tRNA_RF*.txt
do
[ -e "$file" ] || continue \     
name=$(basename "$file" .txt) \     
esl-sfetch -f Rfam.fa "$file" \
> "/tRNA/${name}.fa"
done

for file in DIR/rRNA_RF*.txt
do    
[ -e "$file" ] || continue \
name=$(basename "$file" .txt) \
esl-sfetch -f Rfam.fa "$file" \
> "/rRNA/${name}.fa"
done
```

Next, concatenate all the sequences into single fasta file we can use for alignment

``` bash
cat /tRNA/*.fa > trna_rfam.fa
cat /rRNa/*.fa > rrna_rfam.fa
cat trna_rfam.fa rrna_rfam.fa > tRNA_rRNA_rfam.fa
```

And lastly, we aligned our filtered reads to this rRNA_tRNA sequence, and use the unmapped reads for subsequent processing

``` bash
#build bowtie2 index
bowtie2-build tRNA_rRNA_rfam.fa /ref/bowtie2-build_rfam

#alignment
ref_rfam=/DIR/bowtie2-build_rfam

cd $DIR/prinseq/good
for i in *_good.fastq
do
base=$(basename "$i" _good.fastq)
bowtie2 --threads 4 -x $ref_rfam -q $DIR/prinseq/good/${base}_good.fastq --local -N 0 -k 100 | samtools sort -@8 | samtools view -b -f 4 -@8 -o $DIR/bowtie2_rfam/${base}_rfam.unaligned.sorted.bam
samtools fastq -T '*' $DIR/bowtie2_rfam/${base}_rfam.unaligned.sorted.bam | gzip > $DIR/bowtie2_rfam/${base}_rfam.unaligned.fastq.gz
done
```

### Remove reads from chloroplast genome

For this, we combine the chloroplast genome from scion and both rootstocks

``` bash
#concatenate fasta
cat SB2.1_diploid_chloro.fasta 1103P_c100_k301.pltd.ctg.restart.fasta.fasta 3309.pltd.ctg.restart.fasta.fasta > SB2.1_1103P_3309_chloro.fasta

#Create bowtie2 index
bowtie2-build SB2.1_1103P_3309_chloro.fasta chloroplast_SB_rootstock

#Mapping
ref_chloro=/DIR/chloroplast_SB_rootstock

cd $DIR/bowtie2_rfam
for i in *_rfam.unaligned.fastq.gz
do
base=$(basename "$i" _rfam.unaligned.fastq.gz)
bowtie2 --threads 4 -x $ref \
-q $DIR/bowtie2_rfam/${base}_rfam.unaligned.fastq.gz \
--local -N 0 -k 100 | samtools sort -@8 | samtools view -b -f 4 -@8 \
-o $DIR/bowtie2_chloroplast/${base}_mapchloroplast.SB.unaligned.sorted.bam
samtools fastq -T '*' $DIR/bowtie2_chloroplast/${base}_mapchloroplast.SB.unaligned.sorted.bam | gzip > $DIR/bowtie2_chloroplast/${base}_nonchloro_SB.fastq.gz
done
```

This is the end of read processing, and the remaining reads were used in the analysis.

## Analysis

There are two main analysis I did:

1.  Identify the mobile sRNA, i.e. smallRNA present in scion tissue (Sauvignon Blanc leaf) that presumed to be originated from the rootstock. To do this, we first align the reads to the scion genome (both haplotypes), take the unmapped reads and align to the respective rootstock genome (one haplotype).

2.  Analyse the association of smallRNA reads with drought stress. For this, we map the reads to a concatenated reference genome of the scion and rootstock, perform clustering (both done within ShortStack) and run differential analysis on the result to identify clusters that are significantly associated with drought stress.

### Identify mobile sRNA

First, filtered small RNA reads were mapped to the scion genome using bowtie. the unmapped reads were used to map to the rootstock genome

``` bash
#Create bowtie-index
bowtie-build SB2.1_diploid_plusorg.fasta SB2.1_bowtie_build/SB2.1_diploid


#Map to scion genome
cd $DIR/
for i in *_nonchloro_SB.fastq.gz
do
base=$(basename "$i" _nonchloro_SB.fastq.gz)
bowtie --threads 8 -v 0 -a -m 50 --best --strata \
       --un $DIR/${base}.unaligned.SB.fq \
       --max $DIR/${base}.too_many.SB.fq \
       -S -x $ref_SB_hap1 \
       $DIR/${base}_nonchloro_SB.fastq.gz \
       | samtools sort -@8 | samtools view -b -@8 -o $DIR/${base}_SB_dip.sorted.aligned.bam
samtools index -@16 $DIR/${base}_SB_dip.sorted.aligned.bam
done

#Map unmapped reads to rootstock genome (e.g. 3309)
cd $DIR/
for i in *.unaligned.SB.fq
do
base=$(basename "$i" .unaligned.SB.fq)
bowtie --threads 8 -v 0 -a -m 50 --best --strata \
       --un $DIR2/3309/${base}.unaligned.SBdip_align.3309.fq \
       --max $DIR2/3309/${base}.too_many.SBdip_3309.fq \
       -S -x $ref_3309 \
       $DIR/${base}.unaligned.SB.fq \
       | samtools sort -@8 | samtools view -b -@8 -o $DIR2/3309/${base}_unmappedSBdip_map3309.sorted.aligned.bam
samtools index -@16 $DIR2/3309/${base}_unmappedSBdip_map3309.sorted.aligned.bam
done
```

Clustering was done using ShortStack

``` bash

#clustering
ShortStack --bamfile file1.bam file2.bam ...filexx.bam \
--dicermin 20 --dicermax 24 --mincov 5 \
--genomefile ref.fa \
--known_miRNAs mirbase_vitis.fasta \
--outdir Result_DIR/
```

### Association of small RNA with drought stress

For this, we use small RNA mapped to both scion and rootstock. Mapping and clustering was done using ShortStack. Shortstack also use bowtie for mapping, but has default setting that allows 1 mismatch. We modify the script manually to change the mismatch allowed to 0, according to this thread: https://github.com/MikeAxtell/ShortStack/issues/177

``` bash

#Mapping and clustering
ShortStack --bamfile file1.bam file2.bam ...filexx.bam \
--dicermin 20 --dicermax 24 --mincov 5 \
--genomefile ref_SB_3309.fa \
--known_miRNAs mirbase_vitis.fasta \
--outdir Result_DIR/
```

Differential analysis was done using Deseq2, using the count.txt table output of shorstack

```{r}
#Deseq2 library(DESeq2)
#| eval: false
counts <- read.table("count.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) 
rownames(counts) <- counts$Name 
locus_info <- counts[, c("Name", "Coords", "MIRNA")]

#Define samples 
sample_map <- list(control_baseline = c("control1_B", "control2_B", "control3_B"), 
                   treatment_baseline = c("treatment1_B","treatment2_B","treatment3_B"), 
                   control_stress = c("control1_S", "control2_S", "control3_S"), 
                   treatment_stress = c("treatment1_S","treatment2_S","treatment3_S"))

#Biological pairing 
pair_map <- c(control1_B = "C1", control1_S = "C1", 
              control1_B = "C2", control1_S = "C2", 
              control3_B = "C3", control3_S = "C3", 
              treatment1_B = "T1", treatment1_S = "T1", 
              treatment1_B = "T2", treatment1_S = "T2", 
              treatment3_B = "T3", treatment3_S = "T3",)

#Build sample metadata 
lookup <- do.call( rbind, 
                   lapply(names(sample_map), function(grp) { 
  parts <- strsplit(grp, "_")[[1]] 
  data.frame(
    id = sample_map[[grp]], 
    drought = parts[1], 
    timepoint = parts[2], 
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) }))

## Add biological pair ID

lookup$pair_id <- unname(pair_map[lookup$id])

#Identify columns in count matrix 
sample_ids <- sub("_.*", "", colnames(counts_mat_all)) 
keep_cols <- sample_ids %in% lookup$id 
counts_mat <- counts_mat_all[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE] 
sample_ids <- sample_ids[keep_cols] 
dim(counts_mat) 
colnames(counts_mat)

#Contruct coldata to be exactly same orders as counts 
coldata <- lookup[ match(sample_ids, lookup$id), c("drought", "timepoint", "pair_id")]

rownames(coldata) <- colnames(counts_mat)

#Confirm pairing 
cat("nPairing table:n") 
print(table(coldata$pair_id,coldata$timepoint)) 
pair_table <- table( coldata$pair_id,coldata$timepoint) 

stopifnot(all(pair_table[, "baseline"] == 1), all(pair_table[, "stress"] == 1))

## Each pair must belong to only one drought treatment

drought_check <- tapply(
  as.character(coldata$drought),
  coldata$pair_id,
  function(x) length(unique(x))
) 

stopifnot(all(drought_check == 1))

#Split miRNA vs siRNA 
mirna_ids <- locus_info$Name[locus_info$MIRNA == "Y"] 
sirna_ids <- locus_info$Name[locus_info$MIRNA == "N"]

counts_mirna <- counts_mat[
  rownames(counts_mat) %in% mirna_ids, 
  ,
  drop = FALSE]

counts_sirna <- counts_mat[
  rownames(counts_mat) %in% sirna_ids,
  ,
  drop = FALSE]

#Diff analysis, example for siRNA 
count_mat <- round(as.matrix(counts_sirna)) 
coldata <- as.data.frame(coldata)

coldata$ctrl_stress <- as.integer(coldata$drought == "control" & coldata$timepoint == "stress")
coldata$trt_stress <- as.integer(coldata$drought == "treatment" & coldata$timepoint == "stress")

#paired Wald model 
#(trt stress - trt baseline) - (ctrl stress - ctrl baseline)
#Positive LFC = treatment has a more positive stress response

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix( 
  countData = count_mat, 
  colData = coldata, 
  design = ~ pair_id + ctrl_stress + trt_stress)

dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = "poscounts") 
sizeFactors(dds)
dds <- DESeq(dds) 
rn <- resultsNames(dds)

int_contrast <- setNames(rep(0, length(rn)), rn) 
int_contrast["trt_stress"] <- 1 
int_contrast["ctrl_stress"] <- -1

int_contrast

res_interaction <- results(dds, contrast = int_contrast) 
summary(res_interaction)

interaction_res <- as.data.frame(res_interaction) 
interaction_res$Name <- rownames(interaction_res)
interaction_res <- merge(interaction_res, locus_info, by = "Name", all.x = TRUE)
interaction_res <- interaction_res[order(interaction_res$padj, na.last = TRUE),]

write.csv(interaction_res,"res_interaction_wald_siRNA.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#Interaction DROUGHT x TIMEPOINT (LRT method) 
#Fit the design for DROUGHT x TIMEPOINT INTERACTION 
## Full : ~ pair_id + timepoint + trt_stress

dds_int_lrt <- DESeq(dd, test = "LRT", reduced = ~ pair_id + timepoint)

res_lrt_int <- results(dds_int_lrt) 
summary(res_lrt_int)

lrt_int_res <- as.data.frame(res_lrt_int) 
lrt_int_res$Name <- rownames(lrt_int_res)
lrt_int_res <- merge(lrt_int_res, locus_info, by = "Name", all.x = TRUE)
lrt_int_res <- lrt_int_res[order(lrt_int_res$padj, na.last = TRUE),]

write.csv(lrt_int_res,"res_interaction_LRT_siRNA.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#Interaction DROUGHT x TIMEPOINT INTERACTION (LfcShrink method) 
## Full : ~ pair_id + timepoint + trt_stress

res_int_shrunk <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "trt_stress", type = "apeglm") 
summary(res_int_shrunk)

res_int_shrunk_df <- as.data.frame(res_int_shrunk) 
res_int_shrunk_df$Name <- rownames(res_int_shrunk_df)
res_int_shrunk_df <- merge(res_int_shrunk_df, locus_info, by = "Name", all.x = TRUE)
res_int_shrunk_df <- res_int_shrunk_df[order(res_int_shrunk_df$padj, na.last = TRUE),]

write.csv(res_int_shrunk_df,"res_interaction_shrunk_siRNA.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
